rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose noun for a one-piece skirted garment worn mainly by women or girls.

example.english: This dress really suits you—wear it to the banquet.
example.traditional: 呢條連身裙好啱你，去飲宴著啦。
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 lin4 san1 kwan4 hou2 ngaam1 nei5 heoi3 jam2 jin3 zoek3 laa1

rows.note: Use 著衫 as the all-purpose choice for putting clothes on yourself.

example.english: When I wake up in the morning, I dress and leave the house.
example.traditional: 我朝早瞓醒就著衫出門口。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ziu1 zou2 fan3 seng2 zau6 zoek3 saam1 ceot1 mun4 hau2

rows.note: Use this construction when dressing another person, child, doll, or mannequin rather than dressing yourself.

example.english: I dress the little one every day.
example.traditional: 我每日都幫個細路著衫。
example.jyutping: ngo5 mui5 jat6 dou1 bong1 go3 sai3 lou6 zoek3 saam1

rows.note: Use this when dress means formalwear for a special occasion or other formal setting.

example.english: The company anniversary dinner requires everyone to wear formal dress.
example.traditional: 公司周年晚宴要求大家著禮服。
example.jyutping: gung1 si1 zau1 nin4 maan5 jin3 jiu1 kau4 daai6 gaa1 zoek3 lai5 fuk6

rows.note: Use 準備 when dress means to prepare something for use or get it ready.

example.english: I usually dress the salad just before we eat.
example.traditional: 我通常食之前先準備個沙律。
example.jyutping: ngo5 tung1 soeng4 sik6 zi1 cin4 sin1 zeon2 bei6 go3 saa1 leot6

rows.note: Use 敷藥 when applying medicine or a dressing to a wound.

example.english: Clean the wound before you dress it.
example.jyutping: soeng1 hau2 sai2 gon1 zeng6 sin1 fu1 joek6
